# Loop: pace the work against the finite driver allotments
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #72, sha256:294970b50ae7122017fbf7c29ac1edf6e9e5d5b4b674b5cd9e4256b5236124d2). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready (rank: see `C:\Users\ringe\projects\phrase-lang\board\MILESTONE-usable-v1.md`, read-only)
- **Type:** tooling (thin slice; the code lives in mob-defaults; authored by the driver rotation and reviewed by a non-author under D15, with the smoke run)
- **Milestone:** process: the loop runner (continuous, never ends)
- **Source:** product direction, 2026-10-26: the team finds its own features to add, so the loop is continuous and never ends. The loop stops only for a STOP file or the product owner saying stop, a one-way door that needs the product owner's OK, or a driver allotment running out. Part of the loop design, Decider D23 and its amendment D24.
- **Depends on:** 066
- **Story:** As Steve, I want the loop to rotate around depleted drivers and pause safely when all allotments are exhausted, so that I can keep the mob productive without unapproved spend.
- **One observable behaviour:** The loop tracks each driver's usage against its allotment, rotates away from a nearly empty driver, and pauses without ending when all are out.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then per-driver usage (estimated tokens and turns from the run logs) is recorded per turn and compared with a configured allotment per driver
  2. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then a driver near its allotment is skipped in the rotation for new turns; when every driver is out the loop pauses with a heartbeat and starts no paid turn, and resumes when the configuration says the allotment refreshed
  3. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then spend beyond the prepaid allotments is never started: it is a one-way door written to the Needs-product-owner file; the counter-metric (cards landed per allotment) is reported in the published MOB.md

## Context

- pacing and budget-awareness as part of the design (the product owner): the prepaid allotments are finite, so pacing is a counter-metric and a safety guard together.
- The loop stops ONLY for a STOP file or the product owner saying stop, a one-way door that needs the product owner, or a driver allotment running out (which pauses it). Safety rules apply in full.
